cases.title: Mission board drops task context
cases.problem: On the mission board, a mission-level check task (a final verification, a per-criterion check or an acceptance-test run) shows up as an ordinary cell in the build bar, when it should be treated as a helper run and left out. The helper-run and deliverable-role logic reads markers from a task's `context`, but the function that converts a loaded task row into the board's task input (`toBoardTaskInput` in `apps/web/src/lib/mission-board.ts`) never passes the context along. Make the conversion forward the task's context. The mission page loads that same column under the name `contextDigest`; use it when `context` is absent.

reference.subject: fix(mission-board): forward task context through toBoardTaskInput (#5817)

cases.expected: Task input built from a row with `context` carries it through; a row with only `contextDigest` carries that instead; helper markers then classify the task as a helper run.
cases.contamination: Replayed from this repository's public history; a model may have seen the fix or its tests in training. Replay evidence only, not an uncontaminated generalisation claim.

cases.title: Decision card names the tasks waiting on it
cases.problem: A decision card in the Needs You list builds its summary from the question's context text only, so a person cannot tell what is blocked on their answer. Extend `decisionFromQuestion` in `apps/web/src/lib/needs-you-card.ts` with an optional input `dependents`, a list of task names that wait on the decision. When there are names, append one sentence to the summary naming them: one name reads `<name> waits on this.`, several read `<a>, <b> and <c> wait on this.` Collapse whitespace inside each name and ignore empty names. With no names the summary is unchanged, and when there is no context text the summary is just the waiting sentence. A summary with neither stays null.

reference.subject: fix(needs-you): name what waits on a decision in its summary (#5808)

cases.expected: Summary is the context sentence followed, when present, by the waiting sentence; unchanged without dependents.

cases.title: Approving a plan on a coordinate-only mission
cases.problem: A mission can be marked coordinate-only (the stored flag `decompositionSkipped`), meaning the planning agent must not break the goal into tasks. The planning prompt says so, but if the agent returns a plan anyway, `approvePlan` in `apps/web/src/lib/approve-plan.ts` creates the child tasks without checking the flag. Enforce it there: when the planning task belongs to a mission with `decompositionSkipped` set and the planning task's `creationSource` is `orchestrator`, drop every plan step instead of creating tasks, reporting each one in the dropped-steps list with reason `coordinate_only` (extend the reason type). A plan filed by a person or another source is not a decomposition and must still be approved normally, and missions without the flag are unaffected.

reference.subject: fix(missions): approvePlan honours the persisted decompositionSkipped flag (#5804)

cases.expected: Orchestrator plan on a coordinate-only mission creates no tasks and lists each step as dropped with coordinate_only; other plans unchanged.

cases.title: One definition of a finished build (rejected at admission)
cases.problem: Three places decide whether a mission's build is finished and each uses its own rule, so they disagree. The mission card (`completionAttempted` in `apps/web/src/lib/mission-card-view.ts`) uses `progress >= 100`; the criteria evaluation (`buildDone` in `apps/web/src/lib/mission-criteria-eval.ts`) uses `!hasPendingDeliverableWork(tasks)`; and the re-verify trigger (`recheckReason` in `apps/web/src/lib/mission-verify-recheck.ts`) checks that every non-cancelled build deliverable is completed or is the task that just merged. A shared predicate `isBuildComplete` already exists in `apps/web/src/lib/mission-checks.ts`, taking `{ done, total }` deliverable counts, and `missionDeliverableCounts` in `apps/web/src/lib/mission-pulse.ts` computes those counts. Route all three decisions through `isBuildComplete`. For the criteria evaluation, the task rows it loads must carry the columns the counting needs to tell build work from repair, verification and maintenance work (the task's `context` and `roleSlug`). Keep behaviour otherwise the same.

reference.subject: fix: one isBuildComplete predicate for card gate, re-verify trigger and final-verification dispatch (#5809)

cases.expected: Final verification is dispatched once build deliverables are complete even if repair or verification tasks remain pending; the card and re-verify trigger agree with the same predicate.

cases.title: Connector login that cannot renew itself is not explained
cases.problem: When a person connects an OAuth connector whose provider issues no refresh token, the login silently expires later with no explanation. Fix it in two places. (1) The connector OAuth callback route (`apps/web/src/app/api/connectors/callback/route.ts`): when the token response has no `refresh_token`, add a `no_refresh_hours` query parameter to the redirect back to the apps settings page, set to the access token lifetime in hours (`expires_in` seconds divided by 3600, rounded, at least 1; use 0 when `expires_in` is absent). The existing `connected` parameter stays. (2) `refreshMcpConnectorCredential` in `apps/web/src/lib/mcp-connector-refresh.ts`: when the stored credential has no refresh token it currently just returns `no_credential`. Keep that return value, but first record why on the secret row by setting its `lastVerificationError` to a message starting `no_refresh_token:` and explaining the login cannot renew itself and needs reconnecting.

reference.subject: fix(connectors): say so when a provider issues no refresh token (#5826)

cases.expected: Redirect carries no_refresh_hours when no refresh token was issued; the refresh path records a no_refresh_token reason on the row and still returns no_credential.
